Lee-Carter version of the product-ratio method (deprecated)

Source: R/model-multipop.R
product_ratio.Rd

Deprecated. product_ratio() replaces the functional data models of the product-ratio method of Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen (2013) by Lee-Carter-type factors; this combination is a method of this package without a published source. Use coherent_fdm(), the published product-ratio method. product_ratio() still works and warns (class mt_warning_deprecated).

Usage

product_ratio(ratio_order = 1, jump_off = c("fitted", "observed"))

Arguments

ratio_order

Number of stratum-specific (ratio) factors, capped as in li_lee().

jump_off

"fitted" (forecasts start from the fitted rates of the last year) or "observed" (forecasts are multiplied by the ratio of observed to fitted rates in the last year, per age and stratum; Lee and Miller 2001). With few factors per stratum the fitted rates of the last year can be far from the observed ones; the observed jump-off then avoids a step between the last observed and the first forecast year.

Value

A model specification.

Details

The geometric mean of the stratum rates (product) is modelled with a Lee-Carter-type factor (SVD of its log rates, period index a random walk with drift), and the ratio of each stratum to the product with factors whose indexes follow AR(1) processes without constant, bounded to |phi| <= 0.99 (see li_lee()). Predictive draws add Poisson variation of the deaths given the rates and the exposures.

References

Hyndman RJ, Booth H, Yasmeen F (2013). Coherent mortality forecasting: the product-ratio method with functional time series models. Demography 50(1): 261-283.

Lee R, Miller T (2001). Evaluating the performance of the Lee-Carter method for forecasting mortality. Demography 38(4): 537-549.

See also

coherent_fdm(), li_lee().

Examples

sp <- suppressWarnings(product_ratio())
# the published method:
if (requireNamespace("demography", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2019)
  fit <- mt_fit(coherent_fdm(order1 = 2, order2 = 1), x)
}
